title: The Office
subtitle: Greg Daniels, 2005–2013 · NBC Mockumentary Series
blurb: A mockumentary following the daily lives of employees at Dunder Mifflin's Scranton, Pennsylvania paper branch. The show balances cringe comedy with heartfelt character development across nine seasons. Romantic, professional, and interpersonal entanglements drive the ensemble cast.

factions.label: Management
factions.description: Branch managers and corporate leadership who oversee Dunder Mifflin Scranton.

factions.label: Sales
factions.description: The sales team responsible for selling paper and paper products to clients.

factions.label: Accounting
factions.description: The accounting department handling the branch's financial records.

factions.label: Reception & Admin
factions.description: Front-of-office staff including reception and office administration.

factions.label: Warehouse & Other Staff
factions.description: Warehouse workers and other branch employees outside the main office floor.

factions.label: Corporate & Outside
factions.description: Dunder Mifflin corporate figures and recurring outside characters.

characters.name: Michael Scott
characters.description: Well-meaning but oblivious branch manager whose need for approval drives much of the show's comedy. He departs in season seven to move to Colorado with his fiancée Holly, returning briefly for the finale.

characters.name: Jim Halpert
characters.description: Affable, prank-prone salesman whose long romance with Pam Beesly is a central thread of the series. He briefly serves as co-manager and later pursues a sports-marketing startup, Athlead/Athleap.

characters.name: Pam Beesly
characters.description: Initially the reserved receptionist engaged to Roy Anderson, she pursues art school, transitions through sales and office administration, and marries Jim Halpert. Her growth into self-confidence is a major arc.

characters.name: Dwight Schrute
characters.role: Assistant (to the) Regional Manager / Salesman / Manager
characters.description: Intense, rule-obsessed top salesman and beet farmer who serves as Michael's self-appointed enforcer. He eventually achieves his goal of becoming Regional Manager and marries Angela Martin in the finale.

characters.name: Angela Martin
characters.description: Strict, moralistic accountant and cat enthusiast who carries on a long secret relationship with Dwight. Her various relationships and eventual marriage to Dwight are recurring plot threads.

characters.name: Andy Bernard
characters.description: Cornell alumnus and anger-management graduate who joins from the Stamford branch. He becomes regional manager after Michael's departure and later pursues internet fame, largely abandoning the office.

characters.name: Ryan Howard
characters.role: Temp / VP of New Media / Salesman
characters.description: Ambitious temp whose rapid corporate rise ends in fraud charges and a return to the Scranton branch in diminished capacity. His on-again, off-again relationship with Kelly Kapoor is a running gag.

characters.name: Kelly Kapoor
characters.description: Talkative, pop-culture-obsessed customer service rep whose volatile relationship with Ryan Howard drives many comedic subplots. She departs in season nine to follow a new boyfriend to Miami.

characters.name: Kevin Malone
characters.description: Good-natured but slow-witted accountant and amateur musician. A reliable source of comic relief throughout the series; fired by Dwight in the final season.

characters.name: Oscar Martinez
characters.description: Intellectual, openly gay accountant who often serves as a voice of reason. His secret affair with Senator Robert Lipton, Angela's husband, becomes a major mid-to-late arc.

characters.name: Stanley Hudson
characters.description: Perpetually disengaged salesman who endures Michael's antics with barely concealed contempt. He retires to Florida in the series finale.

characters.name: Phyllis Vance
characters.description: Warm, mild-mannered saleswoman married to Bob Vance of Vance Refrigeration. She eventually becomes chair of the Party Planning Committee.

characters.name: Meredith Palmer
characters.description: Rough-edged supplier relations representative known for erratic personal behavior and heavy drinking. A reliable source of dark comic relief.

characters.name: Creed Bratton
characters.description: Mysterious, amoral quality assurance rep with a hinted criminal past. He briefly assumes the manager title by claiming to be the office manager. Seen in handcuffs at the finale reunion.

characters.name: Toby Flenderson
characters.description: Mild, melancholy HR rep whom Michael openly despises. He is technically employed by corporate rather than the branch, creating his liminal status in the office.

characters.name: Darryl Philbin
characters.description: Capable warehouse foreman who moves upstairs into the office over time and eventually joins Jim's sports-marketing startup Athlead in Philadelphia.

characters.name: Holly Flax
characters.description: HR rep who replaces Toby and becomes Michael Scott's great love interest. Her relationship with Michael develops across multiple seasons; they become engaged and move to Colorado together.

characters.name: Robert California
characters.description: Enigmatic, intensely charismatic executive who briefly manages Scranton before persuading the Sabre CEO to make him her replacement. Serves as a surreal authority figure in season eight.

characters.name: Jan Levinson
characters.role: VP of Sales, Corporate / Michael's Partner
characters.description: Michael's corporate superior and eventual live-in partner whose professional decline mirrors a personal unraveling. Her controlling, unstable relationship with Michael ends badly.

characters.name: Roy Anderson
characters.description: Pam's long-term fiancé at the series start, who works in the warehouse. Their engagement dissolves partly due to Pam's feelings for Jim; Roy eventually finds happiness elsewhere.

coverage_note: The series has a large ensemble. Characters including Erin Hannon, Nellie Bertram, Gabe Lewis, Clark Duke, Pete Miller, Nate Nickerson, Val Johnson, and Hank Tate were omitted to stay within the 20-character cap. The 'Named in passing' characters (e.g., Bob Vance, Senator Robert Lipton) appear only via relationships to mapped characters.
notes: Map covers the full nine-season US version of The Office (NBC, 2005–2013), created by Greg Daniels and adapted from the UK original by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant. Spoiler levels reflect the multi-season arc structure; level 3 events occur in the series finale (season 9, episode 23–24).
